import numpy as np

def q_cal(p, b_c, det_d, p_s, wl):
    '''Calculate the momentum transfer Q at detector pixel (x,y). Here we're employing the convention, k=1/\lambda,
    k represents the x-ray momentum and \lambda denotes the wavelength.
    Input
    p: detector pixel (x,y), a tuple of two integer
    b_c: incident beam center at detector pixel (xc,yc), a tuple of float
    det_d: sample distance to the detector, float in the unit of mm
    p_s: detector pixel size, and each pixel is a square, float in the unit of mm
    wl: X-ray wavelength, float in the unit of angstrom
    Output
    Q: a 3x1 matrix, float in the unit of inverse angstrom
    '''
    # Convert detector pixel to real position in detector coordinates (mm from beam center)
    x_det_mm = (p[0] - b_c[0]) * p_s  # in mm
    y_det_mm = (p[1] - b_c[1]) * p_s  # in mm
    
    # Convert mm to angstrom (1 mm = 1e7 angstrom)
    x_det_A = x_det_mm * 1e7
    y_det_A = y_det_mm * 1e7
    
    # In lab coordinates:
    # +x aligns with incident beam direction
    # +z points vertically upwards
    # Detector is perpendicular to incident beam (x-axis)
    # In detector coordinates: x_det // -y_lab and y_det // -z_lab
    # So the position vector from sample to pixel in lab coordinates is:
    # r = (det_d, -x_det_A, -y_det_A) in (x, y, z) lab coordinates
    
    # Convert wavelength to inverse angstrom (k = 1/lambda)
    k = 1.0 / wl
    
    # Incident wave vector k_i (along +x direction in lab)
    k_i = np.array([k, 0, 0])
    
    # Scattered wave vector k_s: direction from sample to pixel
    # Magnitude is also k (elastic scattering), direction is along r
    r = np.array([det_d * 1e7, -x_det_A, -y_det_A])  # det_d in mm -> angstrom
    r_mag = np.linalg.norm(r)
    k_s = k * r / r_mag
    
    # Momentum transfer Q = k_s - k_i
    Q = k_s - k_i
    
    # Return as 3x1 matrix
    return Q.reshape(3, 1)
